title: Go forth (Genesis 12:1–9)
hook: Abram, seventy-five, leaves his country for a land God will show him
carry: go, and I will show you

segments.voice: Yesterday, Babel: a tower to make a name, and a scattering. Your line was not our name. Today, God promises a name to one man.

Seventy-five can be an age for settling in: the house paid off, or close, a pharmacist who knows your name. Abram, at seventy-five, packs everything onto animals, says goodbye to the town where his father died, and heads out with no address. Not a place he's seen in photos. Just a direction, and a voice that said go. After eleven chapters about the whole world, Genesis zooms in on one old man and his first step.
screen: `SEVENTY-FIVE, AN AGE FOR SETTLING.` → `PACKING WITH NO ADDRESS.` → `THE WHOLE WORLD, THEN ONE MAN.`

segments.voice: First, the call. In the Douay-Rheims: "And the Lord said to Abram: Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and out of thy father's house, and come into the land which I shall shew thee." Three circles to leave, each closer than the last: country, kindred, father's house. And in exchange, a land God hasn't named yet. The map comes after the step. In Hebrew, go forth is lekh lekha, and some Jewish teachers hear it as go to yourself, as if leaving home were also a way of becoming who you are. Second, the promise. I will make of thee a great nation, God says, and make thy name great. Notice the echo: at Babel, people tried to make a name for themselves; here, God gives one. Then the widest line: in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed. Not just Abram's family. Everyone. Third, the response. Genesis doesn't record a word from Abram. He went, as the Lord had told him. He took Sarai, his nephew Lot, and everything they had, walked to Canaan, and built altars along the way. Fourth, how the Church remembers him. The Letter to the Hebrews says Abraham went out not knowing where he was going. The Catechism calls him the father of all who believe, and at Mass, the first Eucharistic Prayer names him our father in faith. The Catechism holds him up as a model of faith: not knowing the whole map, but taking the first step.
screen: `COUNTRY, KINDRED, FATHER'S HOUSE.` · `THE MAP COMES AFTER THE STEP.` · `GOD GIVES THE NAME.` · `ABRAM WENT, AT SEVENTY-FIVE.` · then, large: `GO FORTH OUT OF THY COUNTRY.`

segments.voice: Think of something waiting on you to have it all figured out first: a conversation, a change, a call you keep not making. Notice how much of the map you want before you'll move, then ask only for the first step, and picture taking it. If you pray, you can ask God to show the next part when it's time.
Go forth. Lekh lekha in Hebrew: God's call to Abram to leave his country for a land not yet shown. He went, at seventy-five.
Your line: go, and I will show you. Abram didn't need the address first. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics call Abraham their father in faith; he is named in the Roman Canon at Mass, and the call of Abram (Genesis 12:1–4) is read on the Second Sunday of Lent in one year of the cycle.

chat.says: Did God tell Abraham where he was going before he left home?
options: No. God said go to a land I will show you; the map came after the step.
Yes. God showed him all of Canaan first, and only then told him to go.
No, and Abram argued with God for a long time before he agreed to go.
chat.meaning: God says, come into the land which I shall shew thee. Genesis records no reply: Abram simply went, at seventy-five.

lekh lekha.meaning: Hebrew: go forth, literally go for yourself

Lot.meaning: Abram's nephew, who went with him
